title: Issue with importing exported Excel avatar measurements to another avatar.
content:
Hi everyone, I am facing an issue with avatar sizing. When I export the measurements of one avatar to an Excel file(.cvs), the system doesn't allow me to import that exact Excel data into a different avatar. Could anyone explain why this happens or how to fix it?

![3fa31b41e3c74e78a85cb9600202114b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/8a48395e594145d3b457252c18085ffd/images/3fa31b41e3c74e78a85cb9600202114bimage.png) ![1316d46bcfe945ba9935028ab8c8b59b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/8a48395e594145d3b457252c18085ffd/images/1316d46bcfe945ba9935028ab8c8b59bimage.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi,To apply your custom sizing to another avatar, you will need to save the measurements as an .avs file rather than a .csv. The .avs format is specifically designed for saving and transferring avatar sizes in CLO.
Reply 1: thanks🙏🏻

title: I'm having trouble matching the Base Map and the Normal Map
content:
Hi everyone,

I’m having an issue with my maps in CLO and I’m not sure if I’m missing a setting or if this could be a software glitch.

I created a seamless repeat pattern and then generated all of my maps (color, normal, roughness, etc.) from that same image. However, when I apply the maps in CLO, they do not stay aligned with each other. The placement shifts between maps, even though they were all created from the exact same repeat pattern.

To troubleshoot, I:

  * Double-checked that I did not change the scale of any maps after applying them in clo.

  * Opened a completely new file and reapplied the images, but the same issue occurred.

  * Verified that all maps were generated from the same original repeat.

  * Created a collage in Canva showing the tiles side-by-side to confirm that the repeat aligns perfectly and that all images are the same scale. I did not resize the images in Canva—only placed them next to each other to demonstrate that they match.




I’ve attached:

  1. An example showing how the maps are misaligned in CLO.![be1c92a3e25445d9b90a62ad75acd8d7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/4810d4df5d5c4f8ca8a340a615019a3e/images/be1c92a3e25445d9b90a62ad75acd8d7Screenshot%202026-06-14%20143219.png)

  2. The map images themselves, showing they were created from the same source image.![3782e1319e704bd0868443da652155d0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/4810d4df5d5c4f8ca8a340a615019a3e/images/3782e1319e704bd0868443da652155d0Screenshot%202026-06-14%20143414.png)

  3. The Canva collage demonstrating that the repeat tiles align correctly outside of CLO.![cba20313370747dcbc489942cb60672a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/4810d4df5d5c4f8ca8a340a615019a3e/images/cba20313370747dcbc489942cb60672aScreenshot%202026-06-17%20093506.png)




Has anyone encountered this before or know of a setting that might cause maps to shift position relative to one another even when the scale has not been changed?

Any help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi there! Sorry to hear you are having this issue. But thank you for providing the clear images and also letting us know you checked the scale. Usually that is why layers can become offset.If you could please send the files directly to our tech support to take a look at that would be greatly appreciated. We can then try and see what might be happening.https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/4810d4df5d5c4f8ca8a340a615019a3e include the CLO file with the Fabrics all applied as well as the original texture image. If the CLO file is too large please use a WeTransfer link
content_description: A community support page seeking advice on troubleshooting misaligned texture maps in CLO despite consistent scaling and seamless pattern generation.

title: When Software Becomes a Medium: My Entry for CLO x Vivienne Westwood
content:
QUEEN OF ANARCHY & TORN INTO BLOOM — Behind the Process  
When I first read the brief for the CLO x Vivienne Westwood contest, I knew immediately what I wanted to say. Two looks. Two different sides of the same rebellion.  
Both projects were built entirely in CLO 3D. Every texture, every tartan pattern, every piece of custom lace — created by hand using external editing tools. No AI-generated imagery. No shortcuts.  
Every element of both looks was fully modelled from scratch: custom jewellery, bags, shoes, a theatrical mask, a beret with a veil, chains and safety pins — each piece designed to serve the concept, not decorate it. Makeup and lighting were developed specifically for each look to reinforce its narrative. "Queen of Anarchy" demanded drama and intensity. "Torn Into Bloom" called for something more poetic and editorial.  
I won't pretend the process was easy. My computer cannot run Unreal Engine or MetaHuman. So I made a choice: instead of chasing a tool I didn't have access to, I pushed everything I did have to its absolute limit.  
What you see here is what CLO 3D is capable of when you treat it not as software, but as a medium.  
Vivienne Westwood never made fashion for people with unlimited resources. She made it for people with something to say.  
I had something to say.![b4c95c21ade042c7aa39453a3772c931](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/b4c95c21ade042c7aa39453a3772c931VW15.jpg)![1ee787e5c730439a8ae299dca368bd63](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/1ee787e5c730439a8ae299dca368bd63%D0%94%D0%B8%D0%B7%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BD%20%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%B7%20%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%B7%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%8F%20%281%29.jpg)![78756f0802f542b8adf11d4b291a9168](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/78756f0802f542b8adf11d4b291a9168vw1.jpg)

* * *

![5e9f07faa1ac49e59d3e0ebcad5c9021](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/5e9f07faa1ac49e59d3e0ebcad5c9021vw2.jpg)![9ae658277eac46a1b016c8af0bca953d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/9ae658277eac46a1b016c8af0bca953dTHE%20MESSAGE%20BENEATH%20THE%20FEET%20%287%29.jpg)![7971314308254a1eaa48cc07d4e9a68c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/7971314308254a1eaa48cc07d4e9a68cTHE%20MESSAGE%20BENEATH%20THE%20FEET%20%2814%29.jpg)![605d6f0830ee4660a34325396cf7001a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/605d6f0830ee4660a34325396cf7001aTHE%20MESSAGE%20BENEATH%20THE%20FEET%20%2811%29.jpg)![5d8f5eabb002488d9b89026130a11b0f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/0743d6981fd744a98b0d2db1ba450cee/images/5d8f5eabb002488d9b89026130a11b0fTHE%20MESSAGE%20BENEATH%20THE%20FEET%20%2812%29.jpg)

title: 안에 충전재가 비치는 다이렉트 다운공법으로 제작된 패딩 구현
content:
I would like to create a down jacket with a Direct Down construction, where the insulation is subtly visible through the outer fabric.

So far, I have tried building the garment using three separate layers: an outer shell, insulation, and lining. However, the result looks more like a foggy or hazy translucent material rather than the characteristic appearance of a Direct Down jacket. The ripstop texture, puckering gradients, and other fabric details also lose clarity because the opacity affects everything uniformly.

I have a few questions:

  1. Would it be better to incorporate the appearance of the insulation directly into the Base Color map, rather than relying on actual transparency?

  2. For the puckering around the quilted or stitched areas, would it be effective to create grayscale PNG masks and use them as Height, Normal, or displacement information to generate soft gradients?




These are the two approaches I am currently considering.

I would also like to know if there are any other methods that could achieve this effect more accurately. I'm open to using other software such as Substance 3D Designer, Substance Painter, Blender, Cinema 4D, Houdini, or any other tools if they provide a better solution.

My goal is to recreate the distinctive appearance seen in garments such as C.P. Company D.D. Shell pieces, where:

  * The ripstop texture remains clearly visible.

  * The insulation appears subtly visible beneath the fabric.

  * The puckering and quilting gradients are preserved.

  * The material does not simply look transparent or foggy.




What techniques, workflows, shaders, texture setups, or material construction methods would you recommend for achieving this effect as realistically as possible?

이렇게 안에 충전재가 비치는 다이렉트 다운공법으로 제작된 패딩을 제작하고싶습니다. 제가 시도 해보았던 방법은 "3개의 레이어로 각각 겉감/충전재/안감으로 구현을 하고자하니 뿌옇게 안개가 낀 느낌이고 퍼커링의 그라데이션 표현이나 립스탑 텍스쳐 표현도 같이 오퍼시티가 내려갑니다. 특유의 비친듯한 표현이 잘 안됩니다. " 제 질문은 1. 베이스 컬러맵 자체를 안의 충전재가 들어있는 듯한 느낌으로 가야할까요? 2. 퍼커링은 탑스티치를 png로 활용해서 그라데이션을 주는 방법으로 가야할까요? 제가 생각해본 방법은 이렇게 두가지인데 다른 방법들이 있다면 어떤 방법들이 있는지 전부 알고싶습니다. 타 소프트웨어를 활용하는 방법도 괜찮으니 구현가능한 방법에는 어떤것들이 있는지 알고싶습니다.![b7f97fb8f53542d8bf8587cb45821286](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/deb699946b1b4154a4b409d01749c5fb/images/b7f97fb8f53542d8bf8587cb45821286a_52dcd4eccfb7497cbbfb2cc730f758b4.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: perfect

Comment 2: Hi! First of all, thank you so much for the detailed outline of what you are trying to achieve. I also immediately thought to try with an edited Base Color Map (point 1). As for point 2, I do not know a use case, but it is worth a try and sounds reasonably likely to work, why not? Are you using the Fill tool or working with the Pressure function right now?
Reply 1: Hello! Thank you for your reply. I am using the pressure function to implement the wrinkles on the padding. I am not yet familiar with the filling function, so I don't find myself using it much. When I proceed with method #2, the swatch map itself does not produce the texture of actual filling that I expected; instead, it appears patchy.
content_description: This web page explores advanced material and texture techniques to realistically recreate the subtle insulation visibility, ripstop texture clarity, and quilted puckering effects characteristic of Direct Down construction in down jackets.

title: From Teaching MetaHumans to Creating Saturn Unbound
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/50d13ea895a841e78bcb2c3598f76ccdChatGPT%20Image%20Jun%2011%2C%202026%2C%2004_57_21%20PM.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/a85d273f5085449b8c01703d47f2a170Screenshot_1.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/3b9503b36ae74509b4024c5a1de679d8ChatGPT%20Image%20Jun%2011%2C%202026%2C%2004_57_21%20PM.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/8aa67c6964b04d72866e6d1ac1e2f46aepi_kai.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/6a9b89373dbe4ae98c0f78d2dfb910d5Screenshot_5-removebg-preview.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/cd2d5effb9814d329e149976468be0a61_epi_kai.png)When the CONNECT × Vivienne Westwood challenge was announced, I had absolutely no plans to participate.

I am a CLO educator, and my first reaction was simple: my students will probably have questions, so I should prepare a quick overview. I expected a single live session, maybe an hour or ninety minutes, just enough to explain the challenge and help everyone avoid common mistakes.

I was wrong.

* * *

### **The moment I realized this challenge was different**

The moment I started exploring the challenge requirements, I realized this wasn't only a fashion challenge. It was also a MetaHuman and Unreal Engine challenge. And I had never worked with Unreal Engine before.![75aa6486e2614f1997502f8650ecf84c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/75aa6486e2614f1997502f8650ecf84cScreenshot_14.jpg)

**Accepting the challenge**

My students wanted to participate, which meant I needed to understand the entire workflow before I could teach it.

So I rolled up my sleeves and started learning. Not just enough to complete the challenge myself, but enough to explain it to others.

I installed Unreal Engine from scratch, created my first MetaHuman and immediately ran into all the problems a beginner encounters.![dda63822fc374e8d94842089e4207075](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/dda63822fc374e8d94842089e4207075Screenshot_17.jpg)  
**The beginner problem**

That is when I discovered something interesting. Most tutorials are created by experienced users. They skip the little things. The plugins that need to be installed. The settings that need to be enabled. The checkboxes that experienced users clicked years ago and no longer think about. For a beginner, those small things become giant obstacles. Sometimes you don't need another tutorial.

You simply need someone to tell you: "You're fine. The software really works like this."  


**Four weeks of learning**

Over the following four weeks, our community recorded thirteen separate lessons ranging from twenty minutes to an hour.

We held discussions, solved technical issues, tested workflows and documented every obstacle we encountered.

What started as preparation for a competition gradually became a complete beginner's guide to MetaHumans, CLO and Unreal Engine.

The difference was simple: We documented the process through beginner eyes.![96dc65c1e4e34fbb9f784a6c8819ac1c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/96dc65c1e4e34fbb9f784a6c8819ac1cScreenshot_19.jpg)

**Four days before the deadline**

The funny part is that even after all of this, I still wasn't planning to enter the competition myself.

For some reason, I had decided that my role was to teach, not to participate. Then, four days before submissions closed, I changed my mind. I looked at everything we had already built together. The Unreal scene was ready. The MetaHuman was ready. The workflow was tested. The lessons were recorded.

I thought: **"Elena, most of the difficult work is already done. Now you only need to create the garment."**![462b171ec0f3490ba654e2309733cfa7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/462b171ec0f3490ba654e2309733cfa7Epi%20kai.png)**Creating Saturn Unbound**

The main garment was completed surprisingly quickly. The corset itself came together during the first day. The second day became almost entirely dedicated to lacing. As many designers know, creating chaos is easy. Creating beautiful chaos is difficult. I rebuilt the lacing several times.![bca92448bb9441aa8e1878b69bcc2519](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/bca92448bb9441aa8e1878b69bcc2519epikai1.jpg)**Why the lacing became important**

Lacing has been part of my teaching for years, long before CLO introduced dedicated lacing tools. We used to build complex lacing systems manually. The new lacing feature opened completely different possibilities.

For me, the lacing stopped being just a construction detail and became a design language. A way to create tension, movement and controlled disorder. Vivienne Westwood's theme gave that exploration the perfect context.

  
**Using AI inside CLO**

Another useful discovery during the project was CLO's built-in AI Texture Generator.

I used it specifically to generate seamless tartan textures and quickly explore different color variations.

For this project it became a practical textile-development tool rather than a design tool, and I was genuinely impressed by the quality of the seamless tartan patterns it produced.  
![ea93c4b48d0347adb27e5154899c0e8d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/ea93c4b48d0347adb27e5154899c0e8dScreenshot_27.jpg)![19299479129c407cb6ef61123e558438](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/19299479129c407cb6ef61123e558438Screenshot_28.jpg)**Bringing the project into Unreal**

Without this competition, I probably wouldn't have explored MetaHumans for quite some time. Learning Unreal Engine requires commitment. It requires disk space. It requires time. It requires energy. Most importantly, it requires a reason. This competition gave me that reason.![8b34d62d388843c3831008441f04a5c7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/8b34d62d388843c3831008441f04a5c7epikai11.jpg)**What this challenge gave me**

But even more importantly, my students gave me that reason. They constantly push me out of my comfort zone. They encourage me not to stay on the surface of a new topic but to dive deep and truly understand it.

Because of them, I now have an entirely new set of tools and skills that will continue influencing my work long after this competition ends.  
![127b25890c3749e3986582a419dfdf06](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/e851f9bbf122441aa0a6697a58bf9c18/images/127b25890c3749e3986582a419dfdf064_epi_kai.jpg)**To the MetaHuman participants**

When submissions closed, I was surprised to see around 280 entries. I was even more surprised to discover that roughly 60 participants chose to work with MetaHumans.

Having walked that road myself, I understand exactly how much effort that required. To everyone who learned MetaHumans, Unreal Engine and a completely new workflow for this challenge:

**You are incredible.**

I have liked many of your projects. Some of them are genuinely strong competitors. But more importantly, they represent curiosity, determination and a willingness to learn something difficult. I admire that.

Good luck to all of us.

— Elena Androsova, inst @kazan.tools  
<https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/020b210a9c594ec2a4d1c63d4cfc52f5>

Reply 1: Hi Nadia! Thank you! 😊 I had exactly the same experience. The official 13-minute tutorial looks simple, but for someone opening Unreal Engine for the first time, there are so many missing steps that it's almost impossible to follow.While trying to understand that workflow, I ended up recording about 12 one-hour lessons covering all the missing parts: installation, plugins, project setup, common issues, importing MetaHumans, materials, animations, scenes, rendering, and all the little details that nobody mentions but beginners get stuck on.At the moment the course is available in Russian only. If that's something you'd still be interested in, feel free to send me a message. 😊

title: Headline: CLO 2025 on a base M5 (10-core GPU) / 16GB — will it match an RTX 4060 + 16GB setup?
content:
Hi all — apparel designer here, considering a base MacBook M5 (10-core GPU, 16GB, 512GB) mainly for CLO: garment simulation plus V-Ray rendering for lookbooks.

For reference, I currently run CLO smoothly on a 16GB ROG Zephyrus with an RTX 4060, so I know what "good enough" feels like — just want to be sure the Mac matches or beats it.

Quick questions for Mac users:

\- Simulation on complex/multi-garment scenes vs a 4060-class setup?

\- Render times on the 10-core GPU with the new Metal acceleration in CLO 2025?

\- Does 16GB unified memory feel equivalent to 16GB on Windows, or worse?

\- Any throttling (especially on a fanless Air)?

Mainly trying to figure out if base M5/16GB holds up vs my current RTX 4060, or if I should step up to a Pro chip / 24GB. Honest takes appreciated — thanks!

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi! You can find our recommended specs on our main website - https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/8b5d3d6d11954714acec4e00da68d98d GPU memory 16GM is the minimum requirement now. So we do recommend upgrading to 32 or 64
Reply 1: Thanks 🙏🏻

Comment 2: It is still recommended that you choose Windows. You can consider the 4070Ti. The Apple M series is still slightly inferior. In the simulation of multi - layer fabrics, it is not as smooth as Windows.
Reply 1: Thanks Elio🙏🏻
content_description: A community-driven discussion to evaluate the performance of the base MacBook M5 (16GB) for garment simulation and rendering in CLO compared to a Windows RTX 4060 setup.
